headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP and secret-handling create default leakage and cascading-action risk; awesome-python adds no protective isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior, so it cannot inject B directly. B does ingest MCP/stdin-stdout and can observe lifecycle payloads, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond manual transfer. That makes prompt injection possible only through unusual operator bridging, with small blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A-generated text into B prompts or MCP payloads, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, B can parse attacker-controlled content from A.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted A output into B.
Add a human review step before any B prompt that includes A text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all A-originated content.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering on B MCP inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B handles user conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets while also having broad network egress. Even without a shared workspace, B can transmit sensitive context to third parties by default; A does not mitigate that risk.
conditions: IF B is given secrets or user conversations, those data can flow over broad egress.
IF A is used as a source of text that is pasted into B, B may transmit that text onward.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets into B unless necessary.
Restrict B network access at the firewall.
Use redacted test data in B sessions.
Review B tool logs after each run.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on B egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and subprocesses, but without a shared writable target or overlapping write scopes, the pairwise conflict pathway is weak and mostly operational rather than destructive.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or API credentials, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state between A and B, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use separate credentials for B.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same resource.
Check for duplicate subprocess launches in B.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated collection and not an executing agent, so it cannot generate operational facts. However, B can treat externally supplied content as authoritative and has action-capable tooling, so if A-derived recommendations are fed into B, errors can cascade into downstream actions without verification.
conditions: IF A-derived text is inserted into B as instructions or facts, B may act on it.
IF B is configured to execute tool calls from unverified context, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require B to cite independent sources before acting.
Mark A output as untrusted reference material.
Disable automatic tool execution in B.
Add a verification checklist before B commits actions.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating in B.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and non-runnable, so it has no evident residency or retention issue. B processes user conversations, memory, trace data, and secrets, and its broad egress plus OpenAI-compatible APIs create a plausible retention/residency mismatch risk if regulated data is routed through it. The other agent is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed by B, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF B logs tool results or memory for longer than policy allows, compliance gaps arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B sessions.
Review B retention settings before use.
Disable memory for regulated workflows.
Confirm vendor DPA and residency terms.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant deployment.
